item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract and far more reviewable, although it incorrectly duplicates Add instead of delegating to it.","reasons":["A adds the exact requested Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", preserves Add, validates filename/content, and produces a replayable buffered body.","B explicitly violates scope constraints by adding association fields and eight new exported options, extending multipart machinery, and refactoring global Raw.Do request/retry and body-closing semantics.","Neither implementation routes Upload through FilesService.Add, but A's duplicated request path is a localized defect; B combines the same defect with broad forbidden behavior changes.","A's retry test uses an io.Reader-only wrapper, exercising buffering of streamed content into a replayable body. B has extensive tests, but many verify out-of-contract additions and unrelated retry machinery rather than the required narrow change."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data behavior, creating drift risk and directly violating the required delegation.","The new tests omit explicit validation and source-reader failure cases, and the retry test counts attempts without confirming identical multipart content on both attempts.","Documentation inaccurately describes *os.File as non-seekable."],"risks_b":["Adds forbidden association fields and exported FilesOption APIs, changing the public surface beyond the exact convenience API requested.","Refactors unrelated Raw.Do retry, seeking, Content-Length, and ownership/closing semantics despite an explicit instruction not to alter retry machinery.","Upload calls NewFileWithFields and duplicates Add rather than routing the NewFile-produced body through Add as required; future Add behavior can diverge independently."]}
